thread:
alex: FYI, customer hitting 413s when streaming a giant NDJSON for embeddings. Repro steps below, asking for immediate triage.

lucas: Can you paste the request example + error? 413 usually means we hit proxy/nginx limit or content-length exceeded.

alex: Error text: "413 Request Entity Too Large". They stream ~120k vectors in one file (ndjson), each vector is dims=1536. Using curl --data-binary @batch.ndjson to POST to /v1/embeddings?model=redwood-embed-001.

alex: Sample curl they used:
```
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-ndjson" \
  --data-binary @batch.ndjson \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings?model=redwood-embed-001
```

anita-eng: Streaming an entire 120k vectors file in one shot is likely to blow past our gateway limits. We have a per-request payload cap (soft limit) around 10MB on the public gateway; exact value varies by deployment. Gateway logs usually show `request_body_too_large`.

alex: I grabbed their gateway log snippet: `nginx: *12345 client sent too large body while reading client request, client: 1.2.3.4`.

sasha: Two quick mitigation paths: 1) chunk the NDJSON into multiple smaller files (e.g., 1k vectors per file) and POST sequentially or in parallel; 2) use our streaming chunk protocol with Transfer-Encoding: chunked and smaller logical batches (we still enforce upstream limits). Recommend batching ~256-1024 depending on vector size.

john-infra: Adding infra context: edge LB enforces max body size and also ingress has a 32MB hard cap for on-prem configs. Hosted gateway is tuned lower to protect workers. If you need a higher single-request ceiling for a specific customer, we need an account-level exemption and a terrify runbook.

lucas: For repro, can you try splitting file and using this simple splitter (python):
```
with open('batch.ndjson') as f:
  lines = f.readlines()
  for i in range(0, len(lines), 1000):
    open(f'chunk_{i//1000}.ndjson','w').writelines(lines[i:i+1000])
```
Then POST each chunk. That usually resolves 413s quickly.

anita-eng: Also check they aren't gzipping and setting incorrect content-length. If using `--data-binary`, curl sets content-length = full file size which will trigger early. With chunked upload you don't send content-length header. Example chunked curl: `curl -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" --data-binary @chunk.ndjson ...` but note some proxies strip/deny chunked. Safer: client-side split + sequential uploads.

alex: Customer tried `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and still got 413 intermittently. Their network team confirmed proxy in front of us rejects chunked.

anita-eng: Then recommend these concrete actions for support reply: 1) ask them to split into chunks around 500-1000 vectors; 2) lower concurrency to avoid burst + 2xx verification; 3) provide guidance sample for python requests streaming with generator to send multiple POSTs; 4) if they require single-file upload, escalate to sales/ent to provision Dedicated/Private with raised max payload.

sasha: I'll draft a short template reply with repro steps & a mitigations checklist.

alex: template looks good. Also requested they include first 10 lines of their NDJSON and response headers for failed requests so we can correlate in logs.

john-infra: I'll watch for log hits from that customer IP and mark for escalation if we see repeated `client sent too large body`. If they have an SLA ticket we can fast-track.

anita-eng: Long-term: eng-ml will add better 413 guidance to the embeddings docs and recommend client libraries that auto-chunk by token/size. Filing a follow-up doc issue.

alex: Great. I'll push the guidance to the customer and close the thread after confirmation. :thumbsup:
